deepseek.version_drift_disclosure: The 2026 DeepSeek endpoint returns the id string "deepseek-flash" but official docs (accessed 2026-10-23/24) state the current backend is DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (legacy deepseek-v4-flash aliases retired 2026-07-24). Identical id string does NOT prove identical weights to the E1 DeepSeek arm; CEE is therefore not a same-version reproduction of the E1 DeepSeek model and E1-vs-CEE DeepSeek differences may mix model-version change with protocol change.

gpt.version_drift_disclosure: served id gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14 matches the E1 served id.

unscored_faulted_calls.nature: two live attempts on the FIRST bundle failed in the LOCAL client (SDK ChatCompletion.content attribute bug) AFTER an HTTP 200 was returned and BEFORE any row was written; they were never scored or counted as a cell decision and are not in the 44. Fixed before the successful run; resume logic gave every bundle exactly one scored response.

what_CEE_shows: On byte-identical complete bundles both models accepted all 7 sufficient-positive cases and abstained on all 9 insufficient cases; neither produced an unsupported ACCEPT or unsupported REJECT (0 each).
The only CEE errors were over-abstention on decisive-negative (REJECT-gold) bundles: DeepSeek 2/6, GPT 4/6.

Cross-model CEE difference is small (DA 0.909 vs 0.818, paired delta +0.091, cluster CI [0,0.217] crossing 0, exact McNemar p=0.625, 4 discordant pairs); at this sample size interpretation quality on fixed evidence is broadly similar and the edge runs in the same direction.
bounds_on_claims: Mechanism discussion only; CEE and E1 DA were NOT pooled or averaged and no causal effect size is computed.

The GPT E1->CEE disappearance of unsupported acceptance (7 -> 0) is consistent with complete, pre-adjudicated evidence removing under-acquisition, but T3A-T (full active evidence) already had GPT DA 0.8636; multiple mechanisms (acquisition, single-turn framing, model-version for DeepSeek) differ across protocols, so the shift cannot be attributed causally to a single factor.

DeepSeek E1 over-abstention (63.1% pooled oracle) is much lower in CEE (2 cells), consistent with acquisition/policy contributing, but the DeepSeek model-version drift means a version contribution cannot be excluded.
n=22 / 10 issue clusters, class sizes 7/6/9; all CIs are wide and findings are exploratory.
